fatigue.endurance_prime.title: Endurance limit of a steel (Se′ = 0.5 Sut, capped at 700 MPa)
assumptions: Steels: Se′ = 0.5 Sut for Sut ≤ 1400 MPa, and Se′ = 700 MPa above 1400 MPa. Wrought aluminium alloys: Se′ ≈ 0.4 Sut — not handled by this steel branch; enter the ratio yourself. Based on fully reversed rotating-beam specimens.
method_references: Se′ = 0.5 Sut capped at 700 MPa (steel; recalled)

fatigue.marin_surface.title: Marin surface (finish) factor (ka = a·Sut^b)

variables.name: a
variables.desc: surface coefficient a (Marin surface table, Sut in MPa)

procedure.python:
def _marin_surface(values):
    """Surface (Marin) factor ka = a·(Sut/MPa)^b with a, b from the Marin surface table (Sut in MPa).

    Example pairs (a, b): ground 1.58, −0.085; machined/cold-drawn 4.51, −0.265; hot-rolled 57.7,
    −0.718; as-forged 272, −0.995. These are the user's inputs, not built-in values.
    """
    Sut_MPa = values['Sut'] / 1e6
    return {'ka': values['a'] * Sut_MPa ** values['b']}

assumptions: a, b are tabulated for Sut in MPa (machined 4.51, −0.265; ground 1.58, −0.085; hot-rolled 57.7, −0.718; as-forged 272, −0.995). Enter the pair for your finish.

fatigue.marin_size.title: Marin size factor (kb, rotating round section)
assumptions: kb = 1.24 d^−0.107 for 2.79 ≤ d ≤ 51 mm; kb = 1.51 d^−0.157 for 51 < d ≤ 254 mm. Bending or torsion of a rotating round section. Axial load: kb = 1 (enter directly).
method_references: Marin size factor kb (rotating round section, recalled)

fatigue.endurance_limit_corrected.title: Corrected endurance limit (Marin)

variables.name: kc
variables.desc: load factor (1.0 bend, 0.85 axial, 0.59 torsion typical)

assumptions: Se = ka·kb·kc·kd·ke·kf·Se′. Every k factor is a user input (the surface, size, load, temperature and reliability factors are tabulated values the user supplies); kf covers residual stress, plating, corrosion and any other effect.
method_references: Marin equation Se = ka kb kc kd ke kf Se′ (recalled)

fatigue.sn_power.title: S–N curve (power law): fatigue strength at N cycles

variables.name: a
variables.desc: S–N curve intercept (coefficient a in S = a·N^b)

assumptions: High-cycle fatigue (no plasticity): S = a·N^b on a log–log plot, N ≥ 1. A warning is emitted outside the 10³–10⁶ cycle range where the power law is usually valid; use strain-life below ~10³ cycles.
method_references: Basquin / power-law S–N relation S = a N^b

fatigue.sn_constants.title: S–N curve constants from two points
assumptions: Fits S = a·N^b through two points: b = ln(S1/S2)/ln(N1/N2), a = S1/N1^b. Feed a, b into sn_power to read off the strength at any N.
method_references: Two-point fit of the power-law S–N curve

fatigue.mean_alternating.title: Mean and alternating stress, stress ratio
assumptions: Requires σmax ≥ σmin (then σa ≥ 0). Fully reversed: R = −1; pulsating from zero: R = 0; static: R = 1.

fatigue.fatigue_criteria.title: Fatigue safety factors: Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg, ASME elliptic, Langer

procedure.python:
def _fatigue_criteria(values):
    """Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg, ASME-elliptic and Langer factors of safety.

    For a compressive mean stress (sigma_m < 0) the mean stress does not reduce fatigue life, so the
    four fatigue criteria all reduce to n = Se/sigma_a (the fully-reversed value); the first-cycle-yield
    guard becomes n_y = Sy/(sigma_a + |sigma_m|), i.e. Sy/(sigma_a − sigma_m) with sigma_m < 0. The
    ASME-elliptic relation is even in sigma_m; treating its compressive branch as non-damaging (the same
    Se/sigma_a reduction as Goodman/Gerber/Soderberg) is the documented convention here.
    """
    sa, sm = values['sigma_a'], values['sigma_m']
    Se, Sut, Sy = values['Se'], values['Sut'], values['Sy']
    if sa <= 0:
        raise MechError('fatigue_criteria: sigma_a must be positive')
    if Se <= 0 or Sut <= 0 or Sy <= 0:
        raise MechError('fatigue_criteria: Se, Sut and Sy must be positive')
    if sm < 0:
        nf = Se / sa
        n_goodman = n_gerber = n_soderberg = n_asme = nf
        n_langer = Sy / (sa - sm)  # sa + |sm|
    else:
        n_goodman = 1.0 / (sa / Se + sm / Sut)
        a = (sm / Sut) ** 2
        b = sa / Se
        n_gerber = (-b + math.sqrt(b * b + 4.0 * a)) / (2.0 * a) if a > 0 else 1.0 / b
        n_soderberg = 1.0 / (sa / Se + sm / Sy)
        n_asme = 1.0 / math.sqrt((sa / Se) ** 2 + (sm / Sy) ** 2)
        n_langer = Sy / (sa + sm)
    return {'n_goodman': n_goodman, 'n_gerber': n_gerber, 'n_soderberg': n_soderberg,
            'n_asme': n_asme, 'n_langer': n_langer}

assumptions: Proportional loading (all stress components scale together); σm ≥ 0 for the diagram. Goodman is the usual design line; Soderberg is conservative (yield-based); Gerber fits test data best for ductile steels; ASME-elliptic matches data and includes yield; Langer guards first-cycle yielding (σa + σm ≤ Sy). For a compressive mean stress (σm < 0) Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg and ASME-elliptic all reduce to Se/σa, and Langer uses σa + |σm|. Check that n_langer ≥ n to avoid yield on the first cycle.
method_references: Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg, ASME-elliptic and Langer fatigue criteria (recalled)

fatigue.miner_rule.title: Miner's rule: cumulative damage and predicted life

variables.name: blocks
variables.desc: load blocks [[n_i (cycles), N_i (cycles to failure at that amplitude)], ...]

variables.name: D
variables.desc: cumulative damage Σ n_i/N_i (failure at D = 1)

variables.name: life
variables.desc: predicted repetitions of the block sequence to failure (1/D)

assumptions: Linear damage accumulation; D = 1 predicts failure (some codes use D = 0.7). Ignores load sequence/order and mean-stress interaction.

fatigue.coffin_manson.title: Strain-life (Coffin–Manson) total strain amplitude
assumptions: Total strain amplitude = elastic (Basquin) + plastic (Coffin–Manson) parts. σf′ and εf′ are the cyclic material constants; b ≈ −0.05…−0.12, c ≈ −0.5…−0.7 for metals. Solving for Nf is numeric (the relation is transcendental in Nf).

fatigue.neuber.title: Neuber's rule with a Ramberg–Osgood cyclic curve (local stress/strain)

variables.name: Kf
variables.desc: fatigue notch factor (or Kt for a sharp elastic notch)

variables.name: K_sigma
variables.desc: stress concentration factor on stress σ/S
variables.label: Kσ

variables.name: K_eps
variables.desc: strain concentration factor on strain ε/e
variables.label: Kε

assumptions: Neuber hyperbola σ·ε = (Kf·S)²/E solved together with the cyclic stress–strain curve ε = σ/E + (σ/K′)⁽¹/ⁿ′⁾ (Ramberg–Osgood). Nominal behaviour is elastic. K′ and n′ are cyclic material constants (user inputs).
method_references: Neuber's rule; Ramberg–Osgood cyclic stress–strain curve (recalled)

fatigue.welded_fatigue.title: Welded-joint fatigue (nominal stress-range S–N)

variables.name: FAT
variables.desc: detail category: characteristic stress range at 2e6 cycles (FAT class)

variables.name: m
variables.desc: S–N slope (m = 3 for most details, 5 for some)

assumptions: Nominal-stress-range method (IIW / Eurocode 3): Δσ^m·N = FAT^m·2×10⁶. FAT and the slope m are the detail-category inputs supplied by the user (FAT 36–160 MPa typical). Valid for the design S–N curve; the constant-amplitude fatigue limit (the horizontal knee, typically at 1×10⁷ cycles) is not modelled and no stress-ratio correction is applied.
method_references: IIW / Eurocode 3 nominal stress-range S–N: Δσ^m·N = Δσc^m·2e6 (recalled)

source.derivation: Se′ = 0.5·Sut = 0.5·600 = 300 MPa (steel, below the 1400 MPa cap)
Steel above 1400 MPa: the endurance limit is capped at Se′ = 700 MPa (0.5·1600 = 800 would exceed the cap)
Compressive mean stress: Goodman/Gerber/Soderberg/ASME reduce to Se/σa = 180/100 = 1.8; Langer first-cycle yield n_y = Sy/(σa + |σm|) = 400/(100+50) = 2.6667
Compressive mean stress: the four fatigue criteria give Se/σa = 180/100 = 1.8; Langer n_y = Sy/(σa + |σm|) = 400/(100+150) = 1.6 (returns a value, not 'no admissible solution')
